header.title: Oracula: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Oracula Sibyllina
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's tlg1551.tlg001.1st1K-grc1, from Open Greek and Latin's First1KGreek (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.urn:cts:greekLit:tlg1551.tlg001.1st1K-gr: The text is full of OCR errors (πολνποίκιλον, ἐπωννμίης, οτιβαροὶ for στιβαροί, ἐξαποτῖδαι for ἐξαποτῖσαι, μαλερον). 'Of the most righteous' renders δικαιοτάτου, a singular that does not fit the phrase; with the bracketed [τε] the clause looks corrupt and its exact sense is uncertain. The subject of 'had received' is supplied from the preceding lines (Hades); 'God' is supplied as the maker. 'Reading dreams [and] birds' renders ὀνειροπολεῖν τὰ πετεινά, literally 'to dream-interpret the birds'. Gehenna renders γέννα.

The text has many OCR errors (e.g. ον for οὐ, φαρμακονς, έγγαοτεριμνθων for ἐγγαστριμύθων, ἀστρολογονοιν, ψνχάς γνμνάζοντες, κον φιλοχρημοοννην, ννκτοκλοπίας), read in their evident sense. The dots after πόλις mark a gap in the text. Asterisks after λυπεῖ and αὖτε stand in the text and seem to flag doubtful words. 'Wretched' may go with 'errors' rather than 'men' (ἀεικελίους).

nodes.text: But when [Hades] had received these, then a second time again [God] fashioned another, highly various race of men from those who were left of the most righteous man, who cared for lovely works and fine pursuits and surpassing modesty and shrewd wisdom; and they practised crafts of every kind, finding inventions for their needs. One discovered how to work the earth with ploughs, another how to build; another cared for sailing, another for star-gazing and for reading dreams [and] birds, another for drugs, and yet another again for magic; and others contrived each the various things they cared for: the Watchers, bread-eating men, who have a share in this name because they had in their hearts a sleepless mind and an insatiable body. They were mighty, of great stature; yet they went down beneath the dreadful house of Tartarus, kept in unbreakable bonds, to pay the penalty in full, into the Gehenna of the fierce, raging, tireless fire.

But when the first things reach their end, at once the second will come upon mankind. And I will proclaim it to you first of all. Evil will come to pious men who dwell around the great temple of Solomon and who are the offspring of righteous men; likewise I will proclaim their tribe too, and the lineage of their fathers, and the people of them all, everything with care, O mortal of many wiles, crafty-minded. There is a city ..... on the earth, Ur of the Chaldeans, from which comes the race of the most righteous men, to whom good counsel and fine works are always a care. For they do not concern themselves with the circling course of the sun, nor of the moon, nor with monstrous portents on the earth, nor the depth of the grey-eyed sea, Ocean, nor the signs of sneezes, nor the birds of the augurs, nor seers, nor sorcerers, nor indeed enchanters, nor the deceptions of the foolish words of ventriloquists; nor do they make the Chaldaeans' astrological predictions, nor do they study the stars; for all these things are by nature deceptive, all that foolish men search into day by day, exercising their souls on no useful work; and indeed they have taught wretched men errors, from which many evils come to mortals on the earth, so that they stray from good paths and just works. But these care for righteousness and virtue, and not for love of money, which breeds countless evils for mortal men, war and boundless famine; they have just measures in country and in cities, and they do not commit thefts by night against one another, nor drive off herds of cattle, sheep and goats, nor does neighbour remove neighbour's boundary-marks of land, nor does any very rich man distress the lesser, nor oppress widows, but rather he helps them, always assisting them with grain, wine and oil; and always the man of means among the people sends a share of his harvest to those who have nothing but are in poverty, fulfilling the word of the great God, the hymn of the law; for the Heavenly One made the earth common to all.
